author: silver state times
title: University of Nevada, Reno student reflects on support systems and path to law school
text:
Anayeli Mendoza, a first-generation college student at the University of Nevada, Reno, discussed her educational journey and the support she received in an interview published on Apr. 29.
Mendoza said her early understanding of college was limited due to a lack of guidance at home but credited programs like Upward Bound for helping her navigate key steps such as financial aid applications and scholarships. She said joining Upward Bound during high school allowed her to graduate early with honors and provided opportunities like internships that shaped her academic direction.
Mendoza explained that she chose to study business after realizing an interest in real estate or corporate law. She described the College of Business as instrumental in preparing her for legal studies: “The professors invest in their students and push them to succeed. I have taken valuable courses with faculty who have shaped how I think and learn.” Mendoza added that applying classroom knowledge at a legal practice has been essential preparation for her future career.
Community organizations played a significant role in helping Mendoza see law school as attainable. She cited involvement with the Latino Pre-Law Association (LPLA) and Huellas / La Voz as pivotal experiences, leading to leadership roles within LPLA and participation in pre-law fellowship programs. “Due to the support and community I found through these programs, I was not only able to confirm my interest in law but also take meaningful steps toward it,” Mendoza said.
Reflecting on campus resources such as TRIO, Mendoza noted their impact on her confidence and sense of belonging: “Both TRIO and the Latino Pre-Law Association have had a significant impact on my confidence, leadership, and sense of belonging.” Looking ahead, she hopes to use her legal career not only for personal achievement but also to help others from similar backgrounds access higher education opportunities.
